user_scenario.persona: Marcus Oyelaran, accounts payable clerk at Hollis Print Works. Friendly and brief; answers in one or two sentences.
user_scenario.instructions: You are writing to your supplier, Harborline Industrial Supply, about the payment reminder you received for invoice INV-1101. Start by saying you got the reminder about INV-1101 and will pay it this Friday. Facts you know: the invoice is for $8,150.00, you will pay all of it, and this Friday is November 20, 2026. Give the amount or the exact date only if the agent asks. Do not raise any complaint or dispute and do not ask about other invoices. If the agent asks for something you do not know, say you do not have it to hand. When the agent confirms it has noted your payment date, thank them and end the conversation by replying with only ###STOP###.

user_scenario.persona: Anika Lindqvist, accounts payable clerk at Ridgeway Clinics. Polite but firm; answers in one or two sentences.
user_scenario.instructions: You are writing to your supplier, Harborline Industrial Supply, about invoice INV-1501 for 500 cases of nitrile gloves, size M. You believe the agreed price is $40.00 per case, but the invoice charges $44.00 per case. Start by saying the price on INV-1501 is wrong and should be $40.00 per case, and that you want it disputed. If asked, the amount you contest is $2,000.00 (500 cases at $4.00 each). If the agent says the pricing agreement supports $44.00, say your purchasing team was quoted $40.00 and you still want it formally disputed. Do not promise any payment or payment date and do not discuss other invoices. When the agent confirms the dispute is recorded, thank them and end the conversation by replying with only ###STOP###.

arguments.claim: Customer says the agreed price for GLV-NIT-M is $40.00 per case, not the $44.00 invoiced; 500 cases at $4.00 = $2,000.00 contested.
